subject: Tributary: procurement & decision-path — latency / cost targets
messages:
From: Caroline Mendez <caroline.m@tributary.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo — Tributary requirements and follow-ups

Thanks again for the demo today — really helpful. A quick recap from our side and the key items we need to resolve before Rajesh (CFO) signs off: 

- Decision criteria (what matters to our execs):
  * Latency: p95 target for typical 512-token responses — our internal bar is <= 120ms for interactive UI flows.
  * Cost: goal is to keep inference spend under $120 / 1M tokens for our average gen workload (mix of 256–1024 tokens).
  * Deployment: preference is Dedicated (VPC) for production due to data residency, but open to Hosted for early trials if IP & keys are isolated.
  * Security/compliance: SOC 2 evidence, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit logs are mandatory for procurement.

Next steps we need from Redwood: a short doc that maps who at Tributary will own each approval (econ + legal + procurement), an outline of procurement steps and timelines, and your p95/p50 latency numbers by model variant for 512 & 1024 tokens.

I'll loop Rajesh on the next message after we get your numbers. Attaching our internal requirements spreadsheet for reference (tributary-requirements.xlsx).

— Caroline
VP Product, Tributary AI
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Caroline Mendez <caroline.m@tributary.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo — Tributary requirements and follow-ups

Caroline — really appreciate the clear priorities. Quick recap and proposed path forward from my side: 

1) Stakeholder map (who signs what) — draft ownership: 
   - Economic buyer: Rajesh Patel (CFO) — cost targets + final sign-off
   - Procurement: ops-procurement@tributary.ai (formal PO, invoice terms)
   - Legal: legal@tributary.ai (contract/SLA review and redlines)
   - Security: Caroline & ops-architect (SOC2 / KMS questions)

2) Technical fit / SLOs — immediate ask from us: let us run a short perf/latency sweep with one of our verified model variants under your 512-token profile. If results meet p95 <= 120ms on Dedicated (and preferably <100ms), we can lock the performance line item in the proposal. If you need Hosted SLA guarantees, we can surface the same p95 numbers but with slightly higher burst latency.

3) Procurement timeline — proposed milestones: discovery sign-off (this week), legal review (1–2 weeks), procurement PO (2–3 weeks), pilot (2–4 weeks), production rollout after PO. If Rajesh needs a cost model to accelerate, Ben can share a short econ summary.

Attachments: redwood-sla-onepager.pdf (brief SLA + compliance bullets) and redwood-dedicated-pricing-2Q.pdf (pricing snapshot).

Proposed next steps: 
- I’ll coordinate a perf sweep Tuesday morning PT with your ops-architect — can you confirm availability?
- Ben will draft a one-page cost model with Hosted vs Dedicated scenarios for Rajesh.

Happy to hop on a quick 20-min call with Rajesh and legal if that helps move approvals faster.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions + GTM, Redwood Inference
From: Caroline Mendez <caroline.m@tributary.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajesh Patel <rajesh.p@tributary.ai>, ops-architect@tributary.ai, legal@tributary.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo — Tributary requirements and follow-ups

Thanks, Tessa — Tuesday morning for the perf sweep works. A few notes from Legal/Procurement ground rules so Ben & team can bake them into the cost/procurement summary: 

- Contract preferences: 1-yr term with an auto-renew clause; we will review SLA exceptions but need an uptime target & an escalation path to an SRE contact.
- Data handling: production traffic must stay in our VPC/Dedicated or through a private peering; no model weights or persisted customer data may be accessible from other tenants.
- Security docs: please send SOC 2 Type II report, pen-test summary, and KMS integration notes (we use AWS KMS with BYOK option).
- Procurement timing: legal review will take ~7 business days once we have a redlineable contract; finance needs a line itemized cost over 12 months (monthly burn + committed discount tiers).

One clarifying point on latency: our UX bar is strict on p95 because we have interactive agents. If Dedicated gets us under 100ms p95 for 512 tokens we can push for production early. If Hosted is around 120–140ms p95, we may use Hosted for non-critical backends only.

Rajesh — quick FYI from the product team; Tessa's team will send the perf numbers and a short cost summary. If you want to join the perf sweep or a quick call, let me know.

— Caroline
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Caroline Mendez <caroline.m@tributary.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo — Tributary requirements and follow-ups

Caroline — thanks. Quick answers and concrete numbers so you and Rajesh have something to review: 

- Latency (p95) baseline (our verified variant: rw-13b-opt):
  * Dedicated (VPC, optimized kernels, 2xA100 profile): p95 ~= 82–95ms for 512 tokens (typical load in our perf sweep); p50 ~ 26–35ms.
  * Hosted (shared infra, reserved capacity option): p95 ~= 115–140ms for 512 tokens depending on burst pattern; p50 ~ 40–55ms.

- Cost estimate (illustrative, per 1M tokens of mixed-length workload):
  * Hosted: ~$140 / 1M tokens (standard tier), with committed discount tiers available on >3M tokens/mo.
  * Dedicated: ~$95 / 1M tokens at a 12-month reserved commitment (depends on GPU profile & utilization).

- Deployment note: Dedicated gives you both the latency profile and the data-residency guarantees (VPC peering + KMS BYOK). We can include explicit audit-log export in the contract.

- Compliance materials: attaching the SOC2 index and a short pen-test summary in the shared Drive link (see related_links). We will provide redlineable MSA + SLA template; legal can start review once we share the draft.

Next steps from us: 
1) Run the perf sweep Tue morning PT (scheduled) and share raw numbers + p95 histograms.
2) I'll follow with a one-page cost model (Hosted vs Dedicated) targeted at Rajesh by EOD tomorrow.
3) Legal: we’ll upload the template MSA to the HubSpot deal (link above) and notify your team for redlines.

Let us know whether Rajesh wants a short exec summary call; happy to join.

— Ben Carter
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
